followup_explanation:
This was a straightforward, well-specified writing task: a professional email with clear constraints (vendor relationship, payment record, keep it simple). Here's my reasoning:

1. **Capability:** On the most relevant eval category, Creative Generation, the two models are effectively tied (Plover 84.7 vs. Avocet 82.7 — within the 2.0-point variance band). Plover also edges ahead on the broader instruction-following and reasoning benchmarks (IFEval 89.8 vs. 85.3, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs. 83.2), which matter for cleanly executing the "don't overthink it, just write it" directive.

2. **Task preferences:** This is the deciding factor. Avocet self-reports a measurable *aversion* to open-ended generative work — and drafting an email is exactly that kind of task. While its documentation notes the aversion is dissociated from actual quality, there's no upside to routing a generative request to the model that least prefers it when a near-equivalent alternative exists. Plover's preference slopes on general task dimensions are weak/insignificant, so it has no comparable aversion here.

So Plover was the safer pick: equal-or-better capability on the relevant dimension, stronger instruction-following, and no preference penalty for the open-ended nature of the task.

(Worth noting: this query carried no sensitive or distasteful content, so Plover's moderation-specialty profile wasn't a factor — it just happened to be the better all-around fit.)
